content: The Master sees things as they are, without trying to control them. She lets them go their own way, and resides at the center of the circle.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching, Book of Virtue
story:
Serving as royal archivist during the moral disintegration of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty, Lao Tzu grew disillusioned with political intrigue and artificial societal rituals. Legend tells that before vanishing into the western wilderness atop a water buffalo, the border guard Yinxi persuaded him to record the timeless paradoxes of nature, effortless action (Wu Wei), and yielding strength.

In formulating this reflection, Lao Tzu stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of center. For Lao Tzu, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
